title: 30-day output sprint catalog - Mina Patel
content:
Why I started this: a tight 30‑day experiment to push sustained focus on shipping small, measurable wins while tracking personal throughput and craft improvements. I want a compact ledger I can revisit weekly and convert into a longer habit if the numbers look good.

Northstar/outcome (30 days): increase meaningful output velocity while keeping quality steady — target: +25% PRs merged that close gaps (bugs/latency) and +20% reduction in my average review turnaround time. Secondary: 3 micro-optimizations in serving runtime landed (micro = <2 days each).

Leading indicators I tracked (weekly):
- Deep focus blocks (2+ hrs uninterrupted) per weekday
- PRs opened / PRs merged (count)
- Review turnarounds (hours median)
- Small perf experiments started/completed (count)
- Notes captured (insights that can convert to docs/tests)

Week 0 (setup) — 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-13 - Baseline capture: PR merged last 30 days = 8 (3 were cosmetic, 5 bug/perf fixes)
- Average review turnaround (last 30d) = 46 hours median
- Habit setup: calendar-level deep-work blocks M/W/F 9–11am, Friday end-of-week digest 4–4:30pm
- Tools: personal kanban (Notion quick board), timer (Forest), tiny experiment tracker (Google Sheet row per experiment)

Week 1 — 2026-02-14 to 2026-02-20
- Deep blocks: 7/9 scheduled completed
- PRs opened: 3; merged: 2
- Review turnaround: median 28h (improved by triage + pairing)
- Experiments started: kernel alignment tweak for small-batch batcher (spike code + perf test)
- Notes: found flaky bench due to dataset shuffle; wrote quick test repro (linked PR)

Week 2 — 2026-02-21 to 2026-02-27
- Deep blocks: 8/9 completed
- PRs opened: 4; merged: 3
- Review turnaround: median 22h
- Experiments completed: micro-quantization profile added to bench harness (PR created)
- Quick win: removed redundant tensor copy in preproc path — 7% median token latency improvement on local 3090 bench

Week 3 — 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-05
- Deep blocks: 6/9 (lots of interrupts; learning: protect morning blocks more)
- PRs opened: 2; merged: 1
- Review turnaround: median 30h (regression vs Week 2; due to downstream CI flake)
- Experiments: small kernel reorder rolled back due to non-deterministic perf on long sequences
- Note to self: add a deterministic stress test before merging kernel reorder work

Week 4 (wrap) — 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-10
- Deep blocks: 9/9 (best week; enforced do-not-disturb)
- PRs opened: 3; merged: 3 (incl. 2 micro-fixes and one test-only improvement)
- Review turnaround: median 20h
- Experiments completed: 2 micro-optimizations fully merged
- Outcome snapshot: PRs merged (30-day) = 11 (baseline 8 -> +37.5%)
- Review turnaround moved from 46h baseline -> 20h median by end of sprint (~56% improvement)

Qualitative reflections
- Discipline wins: morning blocks are the single biggest multiplier for output. Blocking teammates upfront and publishing a weekly digest helps set expectations.
- Small experiments compound: many tiny perf wins added up to a visible latency delta in internal bench graphs.
- Failures were instructive: kernel reorder spike looked promising but exposed nondeterminism. The rollback was the right call; add stress harness earlier.

Scoring the 30 days (self):
- Output velocity: 5/5 (beat target)
- Review agility: 5/5 (beat target)
- Technical risk management: 3/5 (had one rollback, learned to add guardrails)
- Personal energy / sustainability: 4/5 (fatigue signs Week 3)

Concrete next steps (next 30-day cycle ideas)
- Formalize a micro-experiment checklist: hypothesis, quick metric, stress-safety gate, rollout plan (1 page template)
- Add a deterministic long-sequence stress job to CI for kernel tweaks (JIRA: JIRA-ENG-4821)
- Keep morning deep blocks but reduce to M/W/F 9–10:30 for better sustainability
- Run a 1:1 review micro-ritual: two mini-pair sessions per week to speed review and spread context

Open questions / unresolved
- Is there a better way to quantify "meaningful" PRs vs small housekeeping? Proposal: tag PRs with emoji or label 'meaningful' for a trial month and evaluate.
- How to scale the stress harness without doubling CI time budget? Investigate sampling strategy and cached artifact reuse.

Random notes to self (bullet scratch)
- Remember to claim credit on the internal weekly scout note (ops-update thread)
- Ship the micro-quantization docs: quick how-to for ops/bench folks
- Follow up with Sam on the flaky bench repro (Slack thread link in linked_artifacts)

Quick links
- PR: runtime/pull/987 (micro-quant profile)
- JIRA-ENG-4821 (stress harness ticket)
- Slack: #serving-runtime — thread Feb 12 re: bench flake

Closing thought: this felt like a manageable, measurable micro-habit — not a sprint to burnout. The scoring and weekly ledger helped keep momentum and made trade-offs visible. If I keep doing this, want to test adding a "teaching" metric (short docs or code share per cycle) so output isn't just code but knowledge transfer.

(End of sprint catalog)
